description:
crate-jmap-cid-types/src/digest.rs:151 and :189 expose two paths to the same conversion: pub fn into_inner(self) -> String and impl From<Sha256> for String. Both consume self and yield the inner hex String.

The canonical sibling Id newtype (crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:109) exposes into_inner only — it does NOT impl From<Id> for String. Workspace cookie-cutter rule says siblings mirror the canonical idiom modulo spec-mandated differences. The From<Sha256> for String impl is mandated only by the #[serde(into = String)] adapter on the type; that adapter could equally be written as into = String via a Serialize visitor or with a custom Serialize impl, eliminating the From impl from the public surface.

What goes wrong by leaving both:
- Two ways to do the same thing on the public API. Callers have to choose, with no guidance on which.
- Diverges from the canonical Id template without a documented reason (see myoss .7 — that decision bead defends the TryFrom-vs-From asymmetry, but not the duplicate-conversion asymmetry).
- API audit (cargo public-api) will show both; future consolidation requires a deprecation cycle.

Two paths forward, both idiomatic:
(a) Keep From<Sha256> for String (for the serde adapter), drop into_inner. Callers write String::from(d).
(b) Keep into_inner, make the serde adapter use a custom Serialize impl that writes self.0.as_str() directly. Drop From<Sha256> for String from the public surface.

(b) matches the canonical Id template most closely. (a) is the smaller patch.
title: Sha256 exposes both into_inner(self) -> String and From<Sha256> for String — redundant conversion API
